integrator_questions: With mass at 0.6 kg, does the controller need less kd or more kp to hold the bend response? Compare the gain margin with the 0.8 kg run.
Where does max_error occur now: on the oval's tightest bend or on the s-bend and slalom? If it is still at bend entry, the peak is lag-limited and mass will not fix it alone.
Does steering_oscillation rise with the lighter robot, and does line_loss_events change on the slalom?

intent: Single-variable test on the iteration 3 baseline (best score 69.18). Change only mass, from 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg. Keep the 80 mm sensor row, 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch, 0.12 m wheel track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.12 m body width and 0.18 m body length. Expected: max_error at or below 0.060 m, oval and slalom progress above the iteration 3 values, and a score above 69.18.
learning: Track series (0.10 m: 53.1; 0.12 m: 69.2; 0.14 m: 60.3) shows a peak near 0.12 m, so track is at its best value. Lookahead is monotone, with 80 mm (the contract maximum) best. Mass is the last untested single variable on the best design; iteration 1's mass change was confounded with a 0.10 m track. If 0.6 kg beats 0.8 kg, the next test is wheel_radius. If it does not, the optimum mass is at or above 0.8 kg, and wheel_radius is the next test.
rationale:
Scores by iteration, all with the same 0.8 kg, 0.03 m wheel and 12 mm sensor baseline unless noted: 60 mm row at 0.12 m track gave 65.96; 40 mm row gave 52.25; 80 mm row gave 69.18 (best). Narrowing the track to 0.10 m dropped the 80 mm design to 53.14. Widening it to 0.14 m dropped it to 60.26. Wheel track therefore peaks near 0.12 m, and lookahead is monotone up to the 0.08 m contract limit. In every run, max_error sits at 0.060 to 0.065 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit, while rms_error stays at 0.02 to 0.03 m. The failure is a transient peak on bends, not a steady offset. Body width cannot change the limit, so the remaining levers are mass, sensor pitch, sensor size and wheel radius.

Iteration 1 changed mass, track, sensor size and pitch together and scored 53.33. Its 0.10 m track now explains most of that drop, so the mass effect is still unknown. Mass has only been tested in combination, so I will isolate it. Iteration 6 keeps the best geometry (80 mm row, 0.12 m track, 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch, 0.03 m wheels, 0.12 m body width) and changes one thing: mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg. Lower mass reduces yaw inertia (mass times the sum of length squared and width squared, over 12), so the robot should correct a bend peak faster without changing the turn-rate-per-track geometry that the track series showed to be sensitive.

Expected result: max_error falls to about 0.060 m or below, oval and slalom progress rise, and the score exceeds 69.18. Risk: lower mass could increase slip or make the robot less stable at speed, which would show as higher steering_oscillation or lower progress on the oval. If the score falls, the optimum mass is at or above 0.8 kg, and the next test is wheel_radius.
